$comment: Token pipeline configuration read by scripts/build-tokens.mjs and scripts/validate.mjs. Paths are relative to this package directory (packages/tokens): sources under src/, outputs under dist/.

tiers.name: raw
tiers.description: Hidden primitives, recreated from the Figma library (scripts/figma-library.mjs): the color palettes (Colors / Base) and the palette switch (Colors / Palette Switch, ash). Only semantic tokens reference them, never a component or the site.

tiers.name: semantic
tiers.description: The tokens components and the site read. semantic/ is recreated from the Figma library: the mapped colors (Colors / Mapped, light) and the Dimension, Effect and Typography scales, which the Figma library applies directly. additions/semantic/ holds what the design system adds (line heights, letter spacing, motion, the icon font, transparent, the focus ring). References raw tokens and other semantic tokens. Platform overlays may override them; modes give them other values (modal).

tiers.name: component
tiers.description: Component tokens. One file per component, root group = component id, second level = anatomy part. Reference semantic tokens only. Never overridden per platform: the component's decisions are the same everywhere.

modes.$comment: Web contexts of the modes. The default mode applies to the selector above and to every element carrying the attribute; [data-theme="<mode>"] switches a subtree to a mode; [data-theme="auto"] follows the user's prefers-color-scheme through each mode's scheme. Tiers reading a modal tier are declared on every [data-theme] element so their aliases resolve again inside it.

css.$comment: index: a generated entry point importing every tier file (raw, semantic, then one file per component) in cascade order, relative to itself.

syntax.$comment: Syntax highlighting theme (Code foundation): TextMate scopes mapped to semantic color tokens, written by scripts/lib/syntax-theme.mjs as one theme in the TextMate / VS Code format that Shiki reads, its colors being the CSS variables of the tokens, so it follows every mode through the css.modes attribute. TextMate applies the most specific matching scope: keyword.operator (plain text) overrides keyword. covers: every token of this group must have a rule. Scopes cover the grammars the site guarantees (CSS, HTML, JavaScript, JSON, shell, YAML, diff, Markdown). Line states (highlighted, inserted, deleted, error, warning lines) are not scopes: packages/components/src/foundations/code.css draws them from the global.bg.code.* tokens.
syntax.name: quantum

modes.$comment: Modes: contexts in which the same token paths take other values (color schemes today). Exactly one is the default: its values are the base tiers, so it has no sources. Every other mode is an overlay (src/modes/<id>/**/*.json) of the tiers marked modal: same paths, same reference rules, no new token, never a component token (a component's decisions hold in every mode; only the semantic values they alias change). scheme (light or dark) tells each technology which system appearance selects the mode.

platforms.$comment: Per-platform overlays (src/platforms/<id>/**/*.json): DTCG trees that override tokens of the overridable tiers, same paths, same reference rules. An overlay cannot add a token or touch a component token, so every platform resolves the same set of paths. Output: one resolved DTCG tree per platform and mode ({mode} in the output path; aliases followed, io.quantum extensions record the alias and the tier) for any technology to transform. Web needs no overlay: the CSS in dist/css/ is its output. Ids come from specs/platforms.json.
